newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-NICKLAUS STILL FIERCELY COMPETITIVE AT 57.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-NICKLAUS STILL FIERCELY COMPETITIVE AT 57.

text.p: Jack Nicklaus is still fiery at 57, not content to play ceremonial golf and still wanting to be competitive.
After a closing 75 on Sunday for a nine-over-par 293 in his 36th successive British Open and his 146th consecutive major championship, Nicklaus was not a happy man.
"It's always very nice to get the ovation on the 18th green but I'd love to come up four or five hours later when there are a lot more spectators in the grandstand and I am in contention.
"I enjoy playing links golf, but I also enjoy competition. Just to play golf is not my style. I love to compete," he said.
"I do not walk up the 18th hole to get an ovation for my golf of the last 30 years."
The American "Golden Bear", who won the Opens in 1966, 1970 and 1978, said he would continue to come to the tournament "if I feel I can be competitive".
That will be the basis on which he will decide whether to play at Royal Birkdale next year, though he has said he will certainly play in the Millennium Open at St Andrews in 2000.
Nicklaus, whose Open career began at Royal Troon in 1962, said he has a problem with his left hip which he expects he will always have.
He explained it by saying that he has only one millimetre of cartilege on the hip "and you are supposed to have four millimetres".
"It does not hurt to hit the golf ball. It just hurts when I walk," he said.
But it could be a factor in his decision to play or not play again in the future.
"I expect the hip will always be a problem. In cold weather I couldn't play because of it."

Nicklaus, who plays mainly on the Seniors Tour in the United States, has turned to alternative medicine to help with the hip problem and almost did not come this year because he plans a six-month course of exercises to strengthen the muscles around the hip.
Instead he will start the course after the PGA Championship next month.
"Maybe I shall have to have a hip replacement in some years time. I'm not interested in it now."
